model_node_inventory.description: StartValue indicates the initial value, when there is still the full lifetime left.
LimitValue indicates when the end of lifetime has been reached.
Indication gives an indication of what is actually measured / represented by the Value of the Variable and the StartValue and LimitValue.
WarningValues indicates one or more levels when the end of lifetime is reached soon and can be used to inform the user when reached.
Base indication type not further defining a semantic
Indicates the time the entity has been in use or can still be used
Indicates the total number of parts that have been produced or can still be produced.
Indicates counting the process steps the entity has been used or can still be used for (for example usages of a punching tool).
Indicates the abraded length, for example of a drill.
Indicates the abraded diameter, for example of a drill.
Indicates the volume of a substance, for example of a liquid.
Interface defining counters for the duration of operation

PowerOnDuration is the duration the Device has been powered. The main purpose is to determine the time in which degradation of the Device occurred. The details, when the time is counted, is implementation-specific. Companion specifications can define specific rules. Typically, when the Device has supply voltage and the main CPU is running, the time is counted. This can include any kind of sleep mode, but cannot include pure Wake on LAN. This value shall only increase during the lifetime of the Device and shall not be reset when the Device is restarted. The PowerOnDuration is provided as Duration, i.e., in milliseconds or even fractions of a millisecond. However, the Server is not expected to update the value in such a high frequency, but possibly once a minute or once an hour, depending on the application.

OperationDuration is the duration the Device has been powered and performing an activity. This counter is intended for Devices where a distinction is made between switched on and in operation. For example, a drive can be powered on but not operating. It is not intended for Devices always performing an activity like sensors always measuring data. This value shall only increase during the lifetime of the Device and shall not be reset when the Device is restarted. The OperationDuration is provided as Duration, i.e., in milliseconds or even fractions of a millisecond. However, the Server is not expected to update the value in such a high frequency, but possibly once a minute or once an hour, depending on the application.

OperationCycleCounter is counting the times the Device switches from not performing an activity to performing an activity. For example, each time a valve starts moving, is counted. This value shall only increase during the lifetime of the Device and shall not be reset when the Device is restarted.

native_findings.meaning: Three layered models and reusable AddIns
native_findings.assessment: Devices distinguishes base device/component information, communication topology and integration-host representation. Locking and software-update AddIns may also be used outside the model; do not adopt one hierarchy as a universal DIM chassis.

native_findings.meaning: Physical device and broader mechanical/software component roles
native_findings.assessment: Device is a physical entity; ComponentType can describe mechanical or software parts, with concrete SoftwareType. DeviceType mandatory inherited properties may contain designated unsupported defaults; node existence does not prove a known real attribute.

native_findings.meaning: Purpose-oriented functional grouping and user interface resources
native_findings.assessment: Groups can nest and reference the same parameter/property/method from multiple purposes. Organizes membership is not physical part-of. Group visibility may vary with state; UIElement is abstract and concrete UI formats are outside Devices.

Separate product and instance nameplate information, manufacturer identity URI, instance URI, user-writable asset ID/name, patch identifiers and configuration revision counter. A revision counter changes for configuration rather than every measurement.

native_findings.meaning: Device health state and multiple diagnostic conditions
native_findings.assessment: Distinguish the five health values from alarm conditions. Multiple abnormal conditions may coexist; condition messages add causes and corrective suggestions. This does not verify physical device health.

Power-on duration, activity duration and activity-start count differ; monotonic lifetime counters survive restart. Counting details are partly implementation-specific and activity duration is not intended for always-measuring sensors.

native_findings.meaning: Support resources and physical locate indication
native_findings.assessment: Support folders distinguish device images, documents, protocol files and UI images. Locate indication distinguishes supported, selected and active visual/audible signals and finite/infinite duration; this is not coordinates or a verified executed operation.

native_findings.meaning: Discovery roots and block mode roles
native_findings.assessment: DeviceSet exposes roots with reachable subcomponents; DeviceFeatures supports related functionality. Blocks are functional parameter groupings with actual, permitted, normal and target modes, not automatically separate equipment.

Connection points relate devices to logical networks/profiles; symmetric ConnectsTo differs from physical ownership. ConnectsToParent indicates the communication device of a network despite its symmetric declaration. Network locks can extend through subordinate networks.

native_findings.meaning: Host representation and paired offline/online data
native_findings.assessment: Offline leading objects and same-typed online counterparts have distinct NodeIds and matching parameter BrowseNames. Online access is a communication hint; configuration identity can be compared with connected equipment, but objects are not proof of installed-device identity.

Direction, initiation, transfer identity, completion and per-parameter status differ. Locked-device precondition, ordered device-specific transfer, cache invalidation, bounded result retrieval with acknowledgment/retry semantics and no automatic transfer retry must remain explicit.

A lock has scope, initiator application/user, inactivity timeout and remaining time; ordinary locks may permit reads while exclusive locks may not. Renewal, exit and privileged break differ; forced release can leave inconsistent state.
